name: Learjet 31/35/36
summary: Classic small Learjets used for charter, air ambulance and target-towing work; the USAF still flies the 35A as the C-21A operational support airlifter.

wings: Learjet 35/36 carry large fuel tanks on the wingtips; the 31 has winglets instead
engines: Two Garrett TFE731 turbofans in pods on the rear fuselage
fuselage: Slim, bullet-shaped fuselage with small windows
tail: T-tail with a bullet fairing at the fin/tailplane junction
Small ventral fins under the tail on the 31 and many modified 35s

tellTales: Fuel tanks on the wingtips of a small twinjet (on most examples)
Small T-tail with a bullet fairing where the tailplane meets the fin
Slim, sleek fuselage with small windows and a long pointed nose

confusedWith.howToTell: The 35/36 is smaller and slimmer with tip tanks (or winglets on the 31); the 40/45/70/75 is larger with winglets and noticeably bigger windows.
The Learjet 35 has tip tanks or winglets; the Beechjet/Hawker 400 has plain wingtips and a deeper fuselage.
The Learjet has a swept fin with a bullet fairing and tip tanks/winglets; the CJ has a straight wing with plain tips.

usCount.source: FAA registry / JETNET fleet summaries (~350 active US Learjet 31/35/36, approx.) plus ~20 USAF C-21A (AMC fact sheet)
